answer.how: The cycle was already present in the first commit that touched these files, the initial import b3ae88d60f. In that commit, MainWindow (namespace OrionTV.Desktop.App) imports OrionTV.Desktop.App.Views and builds every page in CreateView (HomeView, LiveView, PlayerView, …). It also opens AiImportDialog from OpenAiImport. In the other direction, AiImportDialog takes an IAppHost and an AiCliTool and calls AiCliLauncher.ResolveDocsDirectory/Launch/LaunchDiscovery. LiveView and PlayerView take IAppHost and use PlaybackController, OsdController and AppServices, all from the App namespace. So App → Views → App existed from the start. Commit f1bbae77f7 tightened the loop: MainWindow gained a persistent PlayerView field and player-specific navigation (NavigateToPlayer, ClosePlayer, TryNavigateFromPlayerToDetail), and PlayerView started using PlayerKeyboardHook from App. Commit e137971afc added the App-level INavigationVisibilityAware interface, which LiveView now implements, while MainWindow's new section navigation calls back into the views.

answer.why_problematic: The navigation shell (MainWindow, IAppHost) and the pages it hosts know each other's concrete types. The views cannot be compiled, tested or reused without the shell, and the shell cannot change without touching specific views such as PlayerView. Every new page or navigation feature, such as the resident player or visibility callbacks, makes the two namespaces harder to separate.

answer.how: The smell was already present in the first commit that touched these files. Commit b3ae88d60f ('publish source-free OrionTV') imported 21 of the 22 listed files into the single OrionTV.Desktop.Core namespace/project at once. Together they hold roughly 45 of the 56 participating classes, already well beyond a God Component class-count threshold. Those classes cover many unrelated concerns: AppleCMS/MacCMS JSON/XML source clients and URL/episode parsing (AppleCmsUrlBuilder, AppleCmsEpisodeParser, AppleCmsMapper, AppleCmsClient, MacCmsJsonClient, MacCmsXmlClient, IVodSourceClient, VodSourceClientFactory, UnsupportedVodSourceClient), the Douban catalogue client and home/catalog orchestration (DoubanClient, CatalogService, HomeCategoryMatcher, CatalogPlayability*), live-TV M3U parsing, multi-source merging and channel health probing (M3uParser, DesktopLiveSourceSettings, ChannelHealth*), HLS ad skipping (HlsAdSkip), four AI live-translation/STT wire protocols (RealtimeTranslationProtocol, GeminiLiveTranslateProtocol, DoubaoAstProtocol, DeepgramSttProtocol, Pcm16TranslationFrameBuffer), subscription and extra-source import including AI prompt building (VideoSourceSubscriptionParser, ExtraVideoSourcesStore, AiImportPromptBuilder), JSON file persistence (JsonDictionaryStore<T>, FavoriteStore, PlayRecordStore) and settings/paths (DesktopPaths, VodCacheSettings, DesktopSettingsMigration, DesktopSettingsForm, SettingsStore). Commit 0c5495360e only changed prompt strings and did not affect the smell. Later commits made it worse by adding more classes to the same component. fe42a7f077 added LocalMediaLibrary.cs with a new local-media-library concern (LocalMediaNaming, NaturalPathComparer, LocalMediaStore) and extended PlayRecordItem/PlayRecordStore and DesktopPaths for it. f1bbae77f7 added MediaProbeStatus to ChannelHealthProbe.cs, EpisodeLabelFormatter to Models.cs and PlaybackResumePolicy to CatalogModels.cs. The other playback classes (PlaybackFallbackSelector, PlaybackMediaOptions, PlaybackStartupWatchdog, PlaybackStartupSignal, PlaybackStartupPolicy) are most likely in the cut-off part of the CatalogModels.cs diff, but that part is not visible. e137971afc grew PlayRecordStore with history aggregation that depends on CatalogTitleMatcher, but it added no listed class. The end result is 56 classes.

timeline.change: Initial import of 21 Core files with ~45 classes spanning VOD source protocols, Douban catalogue, live TV/M3U and channel health probing, HLS ad skip, four AI translation protocols, subscription/AI import, JSON stores and settings, all in one component.

Added LocalMediaLibrary.cs (LocalMediaNaming, NaturalPathComparer, LocalMediaStore), a new local-media-library responsibility. Extended PlayRecordItem, PlayRecordStore and DesktopPaths for local media.

Added playback and resume policy types (PlaybackResumePolicy, EpisodeLabelFormatter, MediaProbeStatus, plus the Playback* startup/fallback classes, likely in CatalogModels.cs). Greatly expanded ChannelHealthProbe with media validation, bringing the component to 56 classes.
Grew PlayRecordStore with media-level history aggregation coupled to CatalogTitleMatcher, adding more responsibility to the existing store classes.

answer.why_problematic: OrionTV.Desktop.Core mixes CMS scraping clients, Douban integration, live-TV health probing, HLS ad detection, OpenAI/Gemini/Doubao/Deepgram speech-translation wire protocols, local media scanning and JSON persistence in one namespace. Any change, such as a new translation provider or source protocol, recompiles and risks the whole core, and the pieces cannot be reused or tested in isolation. Cross-cutting shortcuts like PlayRecordStore depending on CatalogTitleMatcher, or the settings record referencing Doubao and Gemini protocol constants, show how the lack of internal boundaries lets unrelated features become entangled.

answer.how: The smell was already present in the first commit that touched these files. In b3ae88d60f ('publish source-free OrionTV') the single test project received a batch of fixtures that do not use each other and cover unrelated product features: AI CLI launching (AiCliLauncherTests), AppleCMS/MacCMS catalog clients (AppleCmsServiceTests and VodProtocolTests with StubHandler), live-channel health probing (ChannelHealthScoringTests with RecordingHandler and FlvResponseHandler), settings (DesktopSettingsTests), extra video sources and AI prompts (ExtraVideoSourcesTests), HLS ad skipping (HlsAdSkipTests), home category matching, M3U parsing, subscription parsing, realtime translation protocols (RealtimeTranslationProtocolTests and GeminiLiveTranslateProtocolTests in the same file), and the VOD download cache (VodCacheServiceTests with FakeHlsServer). That is already many independent class groups in one component, so the low-cohesion condition was met from the start. Later commits added more unrelated islands instead of splitting the project. fe42a7f077 added LocalMediaLibraryTests, which also exercises PlayRecordStore. e1991e7308 added MpvLocalEngineTests for the mpv local player. f1bbae77f7 added DesktopUpdateServiceTests (installer download/verification with StubHttpMessageHandler and InlineProgress), PlaybackResumePolicyTests, PlayerShortcutTests (WPF keys), VodCacheLookupTests and VodSourceHealthProbeTests (with StubDecodeProbe). The same commit put five more HTTP handler fakes into ChannelHealthScoringTests. c601eb789d added WPF UI navigation tests (WpfNavigationCollection, PlayerNavigationSurfaceTests). e137971afc added LocalCachePlaybackCatalogTests, PlayRecordHistoryTests, and InlineProgress<T> and BlockingFirstProgress inside VodCacheServiceTests. The files for LocalStoreTests/TestStringStore and for the Deepgram/Doubao protocol tests are not shown in the visible diffs; they were probably in the truncated parts of the initial files.

Added LocalMediaLibraryTests, a new independent group for local media naming/import and play-record persistence.
Added MpvLocalEngineTests, another isolated concern (mpv player argument building).
Added unrelated groups for the self-updater, resume policy, player shortcuts, VOD cache lookup and VOD source health probing. Also expanded the channel-health fakes with five more handler classes.
Added WPF navigation UI tests (WpfNavigationCollection, PlayerNavigationSurfaceTests), mixing UI-thread integration tests into the same component.
Added LocalCachePlaybackCatalogTests and PlayRecordHistoryTests plus extra progress helpers in VodCacheServiceTests, increasing the number of disconnected groups.

answer.why_problematic: One assembly mixes fast pure-logic tests (M3U, ad-skip, category matching) with process-spawning PowerShell tests, a TCP-based FakeHlsServer, STA-thread WPF window tests and network integration tests. Every feature change in Core or App touches the same project, and nobody can run or own one feature's tests in isolation. Helpers such as StubHandler, StubHttpMessageHandler, InlineProgress and InlineProgress<T> get re-invented per file instead of shared, because nothing groups the related fixtures.

answer.why_problematic: Each release commit (1.3.15, 1.3.16, 1.3.17) dumps more fixtures and private fakes into the one OrionTV.Desktop.Tests project, so it keeps growing alongside both Core and App. Its 42 classes cover CMS clients, live-channel probes, translation protocols, updater, mpv, WPF navigation and the VOD cache. That makes the suite slow and hard to navigate, and fragile to run as a whole: a heavy test such as the STA WPF test or the PowerShell launcher test affects every unrelated feature's feedback loop.
